title: Personal Checking: The Debit Card and ATM Overdraft Election
content:
## Clause

The Personal Checking overdraft election reaches only two kinds of transaction: cash taken at an ATM, and a debit card purchase made as a one-off. Checks, ACH debits and debit card payments that recur are paid or returned without regard to it.

- **Opting in** needs the owner's own affirmative consent, given personally by the owner; it cannot be entered for the owner by someone else. It is open only on a tier that offers overdraft coverage, which is read from the tier on the account record.
- **Opting out** may be asked for at any moment on any tier, and it takes effect as soon as it is recorded.
- **Effect over time.** A new election governs transactions authorized after it is recorded. It never changes the treatment of items already paid or declined, and an opt-out does not bring back fees already charged.
- **No change, no record.** Recording the election the account already has changes nothing and leaves no record.

## Q&A

**Does the election decide what happens to a check that would overdraw the account?** No. Checks, ACH debits and recurring card payments fall outside it.

**Can an owner of a tier without overdraft coverage opt in?** No. Opting in exists only where the tier offers coverage; opting out remains possible everywhere.

**An owner opted out yesterday. Is an overdraft fee charged last week refunded because of it?** No; an opt-out looks forward only.

**The account already shows opted in and the owner asks to opt in again. What changes?** Nothing; no new record arises.
